html:
The Illyrians were Indo-European peoples of the western Balkans, along the Adriatic coast in what is now Albania, Montenegro, Croatia, Bosnia and Serbia. The map shows them from 1500 to 500 BCE.

"Illyrians" was a name the Greeks gave to their northern neighbours, many separate tribes who may never have called themselves by one name. With the Thracians and the Greeks they were one of the three main peoples of the ancient Balkans. They lived in hillforts, farmed and herded, and some coastal tribes were skilled sailors and pirates in fast light ships.

Illyrian kingdoms grew in the 400s and 300s BCE and fought Macedon; Philip II defeated the Illyrian king Bardylis in 358 BCE. Later the Ardiaean kingdom, under Queen Teuta, preyed on Italian shipping, which brought on the first of the Illyrian Wars with Rome in 229 BCE. Rome took the last kingdom in 168 BCE, and after a great revolt from 6 to 9 CE the region became the province of Illyricum. Several later Roman emperors, among them Diocletian, came from these lands.
